body:
I tend to disagree, we had this request before and there are arguments against it:
- https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/pull/7818#issuecomment-84474283
- https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/pull/829

@samdark please re-check the decision.

I've read those and I get the point. The general use case for loginUrl=NULL is for a standalone restful API, which is stateless and every request should be authenticated, therefore 403 is appropriate.

My current use case is that I have a restful-style API for an AJAX application, that does have state. In that case I want to differentiate between unauthorized and unauthenticated. I definitely do not want to redirect my AJAX requests. In this case, 403 definitely doesn't fit the bill. I'm not quite sure what the correct response is, but that's my problem. Just explaining how I came to report this.

I'm happy for you to revert the change.

issue.title: User component should respect Accept header.

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
When using certain kinds of requests, like AJAX, it makes no sense to send a redirect to the login page.
For AJAX requests Yii handles this by throwing a forbidden exception, returning `403`.

Some non-AJAX requests don't accept `text/html` and it doesn't ever make sense to redirect them to the login page.
One such example is an `EventSource` (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventSource).

In conclusion, currently the redirect to the login page is incorrect when `text/html` is not `acceptable` (ie, mentioned explicitly, via `*` or by omission of the `Accept` header).

In such cases it makes more sense to throw a `401 Unauthorized` error than to redirect the user to a page that does not fill the request specifications (and that should actually throw a `406 Not Acceptable` instead of just blindly serving `text/html`.

Side note, for AJAX request, this code makes no sense:

```
throw new ForbiddenHttpException(Yii::t('yii', 'Login Required'));
```

If login is required the code should be `401` not `403`.

issue.title: yii\web\User::loginRequired() should use UnauthorizedHttpException instead of ForbiddenHttpException

### What steps will reproduce the problem?
ajax request call `yii\web\User::loginRequired()` to throw a `ForbiddenHttpException`

### What is the expected result?
throw a `UnauthorizedHttpException`

### What do you get instead?
let the client handle the non logged in interaction better

### Additional info

| Q                | A
| ---------------- | ---
| Yii version      | 2.0.14
| PHP version      | 7.1.12
| Operating system | Centos 7.0
